svg.title: Finite fixed corners and the centre test
svg.desc: A finite matrix cutoff and its involutive image have a finite fixed join. An outer free-group character involution fixes all original cutoffs while every two-by-two exchange algebra remains a factor. Through an actual ambient isomorphism, one such finite centre test detects innerness of the coefficient exchange.

g.text: Finite fixed corners do not by themselves make an exchange inner
M = B(ℓ²ℕ) ⊗̄ N, N = L(F∞) on countably many generators; T = Tr ⊗ τ.
1. Any normal involution γ gives an increasing finite fixed exhaustion
qₙ = Σⱼ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹ Eⱼⱼ ⊗ 1
Each single diagonal corner is N.
T(qₙ) = n; T(γ(qₙ)) < ∞.
eₙ = qₙ ∨ γ(qₙ)
γ(eₙ) = eₙ; eₙ ↑ 1 strongly.
qₙ and γ(qₙ) need not commute.
n ≤ T(eₙ) ≤ n + T(γ(qₙ)) < ∞
Polar part of (1 − qₙ)γ(qₙ):
vv* = eₙ − qₙ; v*v ≤ γ(qₙ).
γ inner ⇔ γ restricted to eₙMeₙ inner ⇔ C(γ restricted to eₙMeₙ) is not a factor.
Lemma 5K.1; Proposition 5K.2. Corner trace: Lemma 5J.2(2). Innerness: Propositions 5I.1 and 5I.5.
2. A fixed finite exhaustion can coexist with an outer involution
χ(a₀) = −1; χ(aⱼ) = 1 for j ≥ 1. α(λg) = χ(g)λg; γ = id ⊗ α.
Every cutoff is fixed: eₙ = qₙ and T(eₙ) = n. Every finite exchange algebra C(γ|qₙMqₙ) is a factor.
A putative implementer w ∈ N commutes with each tail generator. Choose b absent from a word g ≠ 1.
The distinct words bᵏgb⁻ᵏ have equal Fourier coefficients. Square summability forces each to vanish.
Example 5K.3 and Exercise 6.38: w would be scalar, contradicting α(λa₀) = −λa₀.
3. Keep the actual normal onto ambient map Θ
B(L) ⊗̄ B(L) ⊗̄ R ──Θ──→ M; γ = Θ(id ⊗ id ⊗ β)Θ⁻¹.
A nontrivial central projection of C(γ|e₁Me₁) gives a corner symmetry t.
The full-corner lift gives u ∈ M; Θ⁻¹(u) commutes with the first two matrix coordinates.
Θ⁻¹(u) = 1 ⊗ 1 ⊗ s; s = s*, s² = 1R, β = Ad s.
Corollary 5K.4. This tests innerness; it does not construct R or Θ or establish either relative commutant.
Exact proofs: Section 5K. Quotient and whole-copy conditions: Theorem 5I.3.
Source target: Alain Connes, Corollary 11 and Sakai note, author-hosted typeset PDF 44–45.
